hunt.justification: CVE-2026-21589 allows unauthenticated remote access to sensitive configuration files like crowd.properties, which often contain plaintext credentials. This exposure directly enables persistence through administrative account creation.

meta.name: Atlassian Path Traversal and Administrative Persistence

related.reason: This hunt focuses on file-read and administrative persistence; a subsequent RCE using the stolen credentials would involve process execution and belongs to a sibling hunt.

meta.analysis: A standard rule might fire on the path traversal sequence; this hunt correlates that request with a rare administrative group change on the same host and checks software inventory to confirm a successful breach rather than just a failed scan.

scenario.summary: Unauthenticated remote attackers exploit CVE-2026-21589 in Atlassian Data Center products by using double-colon (::) sequences as path separators to read sensitive configuration files like crowd.properties. Once credentials are stolen, they can be used to create new users and elevate privileges by adding them to the jira-administrators group.

meta.rationale: Start with internet-facing servers identified as running Atlassian Data Center products. The hunt automates correlation between HTTP traversal leads and identity persistence checks on those specific hosts.
meta.hypothesis: An unauthenticated attacker is using double-colon path traversal to read Atlassian configuration files and then creating administrative accounts for persistence.

scope_hosts.description: Specific hosts to narrow the hunt; leave empty to scan the entire estate.

admin_groups.description: Atlassian administrative groups that attackers may target for persistence.

traversal_patterns.description: Specific Atlassian configuration files and directories targeted by attackers.

references.name: Rapid7 — CVE-2026-21589: Critical unauthenticated arbitrary file access in Atlassian products

hunt.name: Atlassian Path Traversal and Administrative Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt identifies unauthenticated path traversal attempts targeting Atlassian Data Center products and correlates them with subsequent identity manipulation. It follows a gated flow: a lead query identifies high-confidence traversal patterns in HTTP logs, followed by an agent evaluation. If the lead is valid, the hunt fans out to assess the software vulnerability status of those hosts and detect any unauthorized additions to administrative groups.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, src_endpoint_ip, url_full, status_code, user_agent, time FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (LOWER(url_full) LIKE '%::..%' OR LOWER(url_full) LIKE '%..::%' OR LOWER(url_full) LIKE '%::/..%' OR LOWER(url_full) LIKE '%..%253a%253a%' OR instr(',' || '{{traversal_patterns}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_full) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify HTTP requests containing double-colon traversal sequences or attempts to access known Atlassian configuration files.
config.expected_signal: HTTP requests showing double-colon sequences (::..) or paths containing WEB-INF or crowd.properties. Status code 200 suggests a successful file read.

config.objective: Determine if the HTTP requests in detect-traversal-attempts show malicious intent to exploit Atlassian path traversal vulnerabilities.
config.description: Decide whether the observed HTTP patterns represent a credible exploit attempt against an Atlassian asset.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign citing the URL and source IP.
config.success_criteria: A clear verdict on whether to proceed with the full investigation.

config.question: the evaluate-lead verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the evaluate-lead verdict is suspicious or malicious for at least one host
config.description: Stop the hunt early if no credible exploitation is found, saving analyst time and compute resources.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%jira%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%confluence%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%bitbucket%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%crowd%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%bamboo%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Verify if the hosts targeted by traversal attempts are running affected Atlassian products.
config.expected_signal: A list of Atlassian software and versions. Comparison with the advisory confirms whether the host is vulnerable.

primitive_config.label: Check Atlassian software vulnerability
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, vendor_name FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%jira%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%confluence%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%bitbucket%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%crowd%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%bamboo%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: A list of Atlassian software and versions. Comparison with the advisory confirms whether the host is vulnerable.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, group_name, user_name, activity_name, MIN(time) AS first_seen, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count FROM hb_group_management WHERE (LOWER(group_name) LIKE '%admin%' OR LOWER(group_name) LIKE '%atlassian%' OR instr(',' || '{{admin_groups}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(group_name) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, group_name, user_name, activity_name HAVING host_count <= 2
config.description: Search for administrative group changes on the target hosts, highlighting rare additions that may indicate persistence.
config.expected_signal: Additions to groups like jira-administrators seen only on a few hosts. High frequency on one host with a traversal lead is a strong indicator of compromise.

config.instructions: Isolate the host immediately. Revoke all credentials that might have been stored in crowd.properties or urlrewrite.xml and force a password reset for all members of the identified administrative groups.

config.description: Final confirmation of hunt findings and audit of credential rotation status.
